title: LLM Kelp-Wald – Faserbündel-Visualisierung der Transformer-Architektur
category_reason: Uses fiber bundle mathematics (base space = token positions, fiber = embedding/layer stack) to visualize and explain Transformer architecture, attention mechanisms, and failure modes (hallucination, circular references).
thesis: The Transformer stack can be understood as a fiber bundle over the token sequence, where each token position carries a fiber (embedding × layers) and attention creates horizontal flows between fibers; failure modes (hallucination, circular reasoning) manifest as topological defects in this bundle structure.
key_claims: Tokens form the base space B; each token's embedding through N layers forms a vertical fiber F
Attention weights create horizontal couplings between fibers, visualized as flow lines
Hallucination = a section s jumps discontinuously within a fiber (topological defect)
Circular reference = attention weights form a closed feedback loop between tokens
Base space topology (line, ring/S¹, 2D grid, sphere) changes the global structure of the bundle
Curvature of the fiber represents 'learned knowledge'; chaos represents entropy
methods_math: base space topology (ℝ¹, S¹, ℝ², S²)
visualizations: 2D canvas: kelp-strand fiber bundle with animated sway
attention flow lines between strands
inference wave propagation
topological defect injection (hallucination jump, circular loop)
base space topology selector (line/ring/grid/sphere)
internal_tensions: The 'fiber bundle' metaphor is illustrative, not a formal mathematical construction — no actual bundle map π: E→B is defined
Attention weights are simulated (hash-based), not computed from real QK^T/√d
The 'topological defects' are visual metaphors, not actual topological invariants

title: Neural Networks as Sheaves — Fully Interactive
category_reason: Explicitly maps sheaf theory concepts (open cover, local sections, restriction maps, gluing axiom, cocycle) to ReLU neural network components, with a full 'Sheaf Dictionary' table and interactive training demo.
thesis: A single-hidden-layer ReLU network is a sheaf: the bend points partition ℝ into an open cover, each neuron defines a local section (affine on its active region, zero elsewhere), ReLU acts as the restriction map, and the weighted sum is the gluing axiom producing the global section (network output).
key_claims: Open cover {Uⱼ} = regions where each ReLU is on/off (split by bend points)
Local section sⱼ = wⱼx + bⱼ on the active region, zero elsewhere
ReLU is the restriction map: kills the section on the negative side
Gluing axiom: ŷ = Σ αⱼhⱼ + β (sum of local pieces = global section)
Cocycle/compatibility = optimizer minimizing loss (pieces rearranging)
The network output is a global section obtained by gluing compatible local sections
methods_math: sheaf theory (open cover, local sections, restriction, gluing)
visualizations: step-by-step forward pass with live tensor values
phase canvas (affine → ReLU → weighted → sum → all)
before/after ReLU bend visualization per neuron
live training with loss curve and evolving local sections
sheaf dictionary table mapping concepts
internal_tensions: The sheaf structure is exact for a 1-input, 1-hidden-layer ReLU network but becomes a loose metaphor for deeper/wider networks
The 'open cover' is a partition by bend points, not an arbitrary open cover in the topological sense
The gluing is a linear sum, not the categorical gluing axiom in full generality

title: Persistent Topology Explorer
category_reason: Interactive TDA tool that explicitly includes Machine Learning as a primary application ('Use persistence diagrams as features for classification'), and the full Rips complex + boundary matrix reduction algorithm is the computational backbone of topological feature extraction for ML.
thesis: Persistent homology provides a multi-scale, coordinate-free, noise-stable summary of data shape: as a filtration parameter ε grows, topological features (connected components, loops) are born and die; long-lived features are signal, short-lived ones are noise. This makes persistence diagrams robust features for ML classification.
key_claims: Rips complex: grow ε-balls around points; connect overlapping points; fill triangles for mutual overlap
H₀ tracks connected components (merge events), H₁ tracks loops (birth at cycle-edge, death at triangle-fill)
Barcode: each feature is a bar from birth ε to death ε; long bars = structure, short = noise
Persistence diagram: (birth, death) points; distance from diagonal = significance
Stability theorem (Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner, Harer 2007): small input changes → small diagram changes (bottleneck distance)
ML application: persistence diagrams as classification features, invariant to rotation/translation/perturbation
visualizations: interactive Rips complex (click to add points, animate ε)
live barcode (H₀ green, H₁ red)
persistence diagram canvas
guided step-by-step walkthrough (birth/death events)
preset point clouds (circle, two clusters, figure-eight, noisy circle, random, triangle)
internal_tensions: The H₁ computation uses a simplified boundary matrix reduction that works for small point sets but is not the full persistent homology algorithm
ML is mentioned as one of four applications, not the primary focus — the file is primarily a TDA education tool
No actual ML pipeline is implemented (no classifier, no diagram vectorization)

title: Algebraic Stacks — An Interactive Journey
category_reason: Pure algebraic geometry education: a step-by-step visual journey from sets to algebraic stacks (sets → sheaves → functors → groupoids → descent → stack tower → algebraic stack). No ML/AI connection.
thesis: Algebraic stacks generalize schemes by allowing objects to have non-trivial automorphisms; they are built up from familiar concepts (sets, sheaves, functors, groupoids, descent) in a cumulative tower, with the final object being a category fibered in groupoids satisfying descent.
key_claims: A set is a collection of things; a function maps between sets
A sheaf assigns data to regions of a space, compatible on overlaps
A functor maps between categories, preserving structure
A groupoid is a category where all morphisms are invertible (objects with symmetries)
Descent: local data that agrees on overlaps can be glued to global data
An algebraic stack is a 'tower' of these concepts: a category fibered in groupoids over schemes, satisfying descent

title: Was eine Mannigfaltigkeit ist — visuell erklärt
category_reason: Pure differential geometry education: a simplified visual explanation of manifolds, tangent spaces, and the generalized Stokes theorem (unifying HDI, Green, Divergence, Stokes) based on Spivak's 'Calculus on Manifolds'. No ML/AI focus.
thesis: A manifold is a space that is locally flat (like ℝⁿ) but globally curved; the generalized Stokes theorem ∫_M dω = ∫_∂M ω unifies the fundamental theorem of calculus, Green's theorem, the divergence theorem, and the classical Stokes theorem into a single statement about any manifold with boundary.
key_claims: A manifold is locally flat, globally curved: every point has a neighborhood that smoothly deforms to a flat patch of ℝⁿ
Non-examples: cusps (no unique tangent), crossings (too many directions), self-intersections break the definition
The tangent space at a point is the unique direction the curve continues in — it rotates globally but is always 1D locally
HDI, Green, Divergence, and Stokes are all the same theorem in different dimensions/notations
The generalized Stokes theorem: ∫_M dω = ∫_∂M ω — the integral of the derivative over the interior equals the integral over the boundary
The hard work is in defining 'd' (exterior derivative) and 'ω' (differential form); once defined, all theorems follow

non-examples (cusp, cross, figure-8) with problem indicators

title: The Jocaxian Nothingness — Interactive Exploration
category_reason: Philosophical/metaphysical exploration of João Carlos Holland de Barcellos' 'Jocaxian Nothingness' concept: a rule-free void from which existence is inevitable. No ML/AI focus.
thesis: The Jocaxian Nothingness (JN) is a 'nothingness that exists' — a state free from all rules including the rule that nothing may arise; since there is no law forbidding existence, existence is not merely possible but inevitable, making the JN the 'ground' (or absence of ground) from which the universe necessarily emerges.
key_claims: The JN is not 'something in which nothing exists' (that would be contradictory) but a state with no constraints at all
Without rules, there is no restriction on existence — no physical law, no logic, no time that could prevent it
Without time, 'possible' and 'actual' collapse: what is possible simply is
The JN is not the quantum vacuum (which has spacetime and quantum mechanics), not the classical nothing (which implicitly forbids existence)
From the JN, anything can emerge: matter, space-time, natural laws, mathematical structures, other universes, consciousness
Existence is the normal state, not the exception
visualizations: animated background canvas (void/void simulation)
simulation modes (spontaneous emergence, with rules, total chaos, freeze)
logic chain (P1–P5 + conclusion, click to expand)
comparison table (classical nothing vs quantum vacuum vs JN)
emergence grid (8 categories of what can emerge)
objections section (click to reveal answers)
internal_tensions: The argument is philosophically contested: critics would note that 'no rules' itself is a meta-rule, and the inference from 'possible' to 'actual' requires a principle that the JN is supposed to lack
The file is presented as 'based on the work of' Barcellos but the philosophical argument is presented as settled rather than debated

title: Origami in N Dimensionen — Interaktive Reise
category_reason: Interactive visualization of Keup & Helias (2022) 'Origami in N dimensions: How feed-forward networks manufacture linear separability' — explicitly about how neural networks use ReLU layers to fold data manifolds into higher dimensions to achieve linear separability.
thesis: Feed-forward ReLU networks achieve linear separability by progressively folding the data manifold into unused higher dimensions — each layer folds what the previous layer has folded, exponentially increasing the number of linear regions; the final layer is the 'single straight cut' (Fold-and-Cut Theorem connection). Bimodal tuning curves are the fingerprint of active folds.
key_claims: Affine transformation (Wx+b) only repositions on the anvil — it cannot create separability
ReLU is the 'hammer blow' — it can only affect the convex hull, not selectively reach interior points
Folding (Origami in N dimensions) is the primary efficient method when layers are wider than the data dimension
Shear (peeling) is the inefficient alternative for narrow layers, requiring very deep networks
Each layer multiplies the number of linear regions (exponential in depth): N^L regions for L layers of width N
Bimodal tuning curves (dip at zero in preactivation histogram) are the fingerprint of a fold separating a class
Causality test: silencing 10 bimodal neurons collapses accuracy; silencing 10 unimodal neurons has minimal effect
visualizations: Demo 1: non-separable data with draggable separating line (2D-egg, XOR, spiral)
Demo 2: ReLU hammer (before/after point projection)
Demo 3: 1D folding into 2D (fold position, angle, count sliders)
Demo 4: 3D folding of 2D-egg (three.js, animated fold progress, orbit controls)
Demo 5: cascade (decision regions of a random ReLU net, exponential region count)
Demo 6: shear/peeling mechanism (step-by-step)
Demo 7: bimodal tuning curves (Plotly histograms per class, dip score)
Demo 8: poker hand results (dimensionality expansion, dip statistics, silencing experiment)
internal_tensions: The 3D folding uses 3 hyperplanes at 120° which is the known 3-neuron solution to the 2D-egg, not a general folding
The cascade demo uses a random net — the region count shown is the theoretical upper bound N^L, not the actual count
The poker hand results are simulated, not from the actual trained network in the paper

Many legends have a 'spark of truth' (Brednich had to admit some of his 'legends' were real)

title: Dynamische Systeme & Konflikte – Interaktive Visualisierung
category_reason: Interactive visualization of dynamical systems concepts applied to conflict psychology from Vallacher et al. (2013) 'Attracted to Conflict': attractor landscapes, feedback loops, coupled ODEs for cooperation/competition, escalation dynamics, and conflict spread. No ML/AI focus.
thesis: Conflicts are dynamical systems with attractor landscapes: parties converge to stable states (cooperation or conflict) that are hard to escape from; escalation can be linear (proportional) or nonlinear (catastrophic with hysteresis); conflicts spread self-sustainingly (Deutsch's Crude Law); resolution requires changing the landscape itself (deconstruction, activating latent attractors, or bifurcation via control parameters).
key_claims: An attractor is a state a system converges to; depth = strength (harder to escape), width = basin of attraction
Reinforcing feedback loops amplify polarization; inhibiting loops regulate; balance = healthy self-regulation
Coupled ODE model: cooperation-cooperation → both positive; competition-competition → one positive, one negative; mixed → oscillation
High complexity → linear (proportional) escalation; low complexity → nonlinear (catastrophic) with hysteresis (de-escalation requires more than escalation took)
Deutsch's Crude Law: competitive behavior produces competitive orientations that reinforce competitive behavior — conflicts are self-sustaining
Sustainable peace requires a positive:negative ratio of ~3:1 to 5:1 plus complexity and adaptivity for resilience

title: Garbentheorie – Sehen. Spielen. Verstehen.
category_reason: Interactive sheaf theory tutorial that explicitly connects sheaf concepts to AI/ML applications in every section (Federated Learning, Sheaf Neural Networks, TDA, Deep Learning loss landscapes) and includes a dedicated 'Where does this appear in AI/CS?' card in the synopse.
thesis: Sheaf theory — from base manifold through fiber, section, presheaf, germ, stalk, sheaf (gluing), to ∞-sheaf (homotopy) — is a mathematical framework for 'local data that agrees on overlaps, hence glues to global data'; this structure appears in AI as Federated Learning (local models → global), Sheaf Neural Networks (restriction maps as learnable matrices), and sensor fusion (multimodal perception as ∞-sheaf gluing).
key_claims: Base M = ground space (time, input domain); open sets U = observation windows
Fiber F_x = all possible values at point x (feature vectors, senses); total space E projects to M
A section s: U→E selects exactly one value per point (π∘s = id); like a sickle picking one grain per stalk
Presheaf: contravariant functor from Open(M) to Set; restriction ρ_UV: F(U)→F(V) (crop the window)
Germ [s]_x = equivalence class of sections that agree in some neighborhood (infinite zoom at x)
Stalk F_x = direct limit over shrinking neighborhoods (all germs at x); the 'wheat stalk' of germs
Sheaf axiom: uniqueness (locally equal → identical) + gluing (compatible local sections → unique global section)
∞-sheaf: replace equality on overlaps with homotopy equivalence → ∞-Topos; the brain glues lightning+thunder homotopically into one event
visualizations: 8 interactive SVG visualizations (one per concept)
base: time axis with movable open window U
fiber: wheat stalks with selectable point x and sense markers
section: path through stalks (sense selector, wave control)
presheaf: U/V windows with restriction animation
germ: zoom slider showing local equivalence
stalk: colimit animation (shrinking neighborhoods → stalk column)
sheaf: gluing puzzle (adjust two sections until compatible → global section appears)
∞-sheaf: homotopy path between lightning and sound (auto-deform animation)
synopse: concept tower diagram (8 nodes with edges)
internal_tensions: The AI/ML connections (Sheaf NNs, Federated Learning, TDA) are listed as analogies, not demonstrated with actual implementations
The wheat/grain analogy is carried throughout but the formal math (direct limits, homotopy limits) is only stated, not derived
The ∞-sheaf section is the most speculative — the connection to HoTT/Univalence is asserted, not argued
